items.requirement: Define the exact production responsibility of Execution plane.
Document what Execution plane owns and explicitly does not own.
Identify upstream, downstream, and peer dependencies of Execution plane.
Define the authoritative source of truth used by Execution plane.
Document assumptions Execution plane makes about nodes, runtimes, networks, storage, and control planes.
Define tenant, environment, site, and workload boundaries relevant to Execution plane.
Separate mandatory Execution plane capabilities from optional optimizations.
Document unsupported deployment patterns and non-goals for Execution plane.
Assign an accountable owner and escalation path for Execution plane.

Approve an architecture decision record for Execution plane, its technologies (Source-derived architectural plane), and its function (Wasm → process sandbox → unikernel → Firecracker microVM → full VM, selected according to workload needs.).
Translate the source function of Execution plane — Wasm → process sandbox → unikernel → Firecracker microVM → full VM, selected according to workload needs. — into testable SHALL-level requirements.
Define functional requirements for Execution plane across cloud, datacenter, near-edge, and far-edge contexts where applicable.
Define non-functional requirements for latency, availability, durability, consistency, isolation, or determinism as applicable.
Define success, partial success, degraded operation, retryable failure, and terminal failure semantics for Execution plane.
Define lifecycle states and legal state transitions managed or exposed by Execution plane.
Define versioning and backward-compatibility requirements for Execution plane.
Define capacity ceilings, quotas, and fairness semantics relevant to Execution plane.
Define behavior when network connectivity is intermittent or absent.
Define precedence rules when Execution plane requirements conflict with security, residency, SLO, or cost constraints.
Maintain a requirements traceability matrix from each Execution plane requirement to implementation and verification evidence.
Enumerate every API, WIT contract, RPC, event, file, device, hypervisor, or control-plane boundary exposed by Execution plane.
Use versioned typed schemas for all externally visible Execution plane contracts.
Define authentication requirements at each Execution plane boundary.
Define authorization and explicit capability requirements at each Execution plane boundary.
Define timeout, cancellation, retry, idempotency, and backpressure semantics for Execution plane.
Define structured failure codes and machine-readable error details for Execution plane.
Define compatibility behavior when peers use different supported versions.
Document payload, concurrency, queue, connection, or resource limits at Execution plane interfaces.
Provide reference examples and conformance fixtures for Execution plane.
Create automated integration tests proving Execution plane interoperates with adjacent architectural layers.
Select and pin approved implementations, versions, or specifications for Execution plane: Source-derived architectural plane.
Separate immutable artifacts from mutable configuration and state for Execution plane.
Define declarative configuration and secure defaults for Execution plane.
Validate configuration before activation and fail closed on security-critical errors.
Support site- and environment-specific configuration without rebuilding immutable artifacts.
Record configuration provenance, version, author, and activation time.
Apply atomic or transactional configuration updates where partial application is unsafe.
Define automatic and operator-driven rollback for failed Execution plane changes.
Keep credentials and secret material out of ordinary Execution plane configuration and diagnostics.
Provide a deterministic bootstrap path from an empty node/environment to healthy Execution plane operation.
Threat-model Execution plane against malicious tenants, compromised workloads, hostile inputs, supply-chain compromise, and control-plane abuse.
Apply least privilege to every identity and capability used by Execution plane.
Eliminate ambient filesystem, network, device, kernel, and secret authority wherever Execution plane permits.
Authenticate nodes, peers, artifacts, providers, and control-plane actors before trust is granted.
Verify signatures, digests, provenance, and approved versions for executable or policy artifacts consumed by Execution plane.
Enforce tenant/workload isolation across Execution plane execution, memory, state, network, and device boundaries as applicable.
Encrypt sensitive Execution plane data in transit and at rest with managed key rotation.
Define safe behavior when identity, attestation, policy, key, or time services are unavailable.
Emit tamper-evident audit events for security-sensitive Execution plane operations.
Run adversarial tests for privilege escalation, injection, replay, spoofing, escape, side channels, and resource exhaustion.
Enumerate component, process, VM, node, site, network, provider, dependency, and control-plane failures affecting Execution plane.
Define automated health and stall detection thresholds for Execution plane.
Implement bounded retry with backoff and jitter only where operations are safe to retry.
Implement admission control, load shedding, or circuit breaking to prevent Execution plane failure cascades.
Define failover behavior without violating isolation, residency, or consistency requirements.
Provide degraded operation when noncritical dependencies are unavailable.
Define crash-consistency, restart, resume, or replay semantics for mutable Execution plane state.
Protect against split-brain, duplicate ownership, stale controllers, or duplicate execution where relevant.
Provide quarantine, freeze, disable, or isolation controls for unsafe Execution plane behavior.
Run fault-injection tests proving Execution plane recovery against documented objectives.
Establish reproducible baselines for Execution plane latency, throughput, startup, CPU, memory, storage, network, and power overhead.
Define p50, p95, p99, and worst-case performance thresholds for Execution plane.
Measure Execution plane under steady load, burst load, overload, scale-out, scale-in, and recovery.
Measure per-workload and per-tenant overhead introduced by Execution plane.
Identify avoidable serialization, copies, context switches, network hops, duplicated images, or duplicated state in Execution plane.
Apply locality, caching, direct composition, batching, zero-copy, or kernel-bypass optimizations where semantics permit.
Bound memory growth, queue depth, buffer size, concurrency, and resource fan-out.
Measure power and thermal impact on constrained edge nodes where relevant.
Define capacity models and saturation signals that predict when Execution plane needs more resources.
Block releases that regress approved Execution plane startup, density, throughput, or tail-latency thresholds.
Expose Execution plane health, readiness, version, configuration, dependency status, and active capability set.
Emit structured metrics for rate, errors, latency, saturation, backlog, and resource use.
Emit structured logs with stable node, tenant, workload, component, and operation identifiers.
Propagate trace context across all relevant Execution plane boundaries.
Expose high-cardinality diagnostic detail safely without leaking tenant or secret data.
Record the reason for every automated decision made by Execution plane.
Provide an operator-readable explain view linking decisions to input state, policies, topology, and constraints.
Correlate Execution plane events with application release lineage and the live infrastructure graph.
Define telemetry retention, sampling, privacy, and export policy.
Create dashboards and alerts distinguishing ordinary load, degradation, policy rejection, dependency failure, attack, and software defect.
Create unit tests for deterministic Execution plane logic and state transitions.
Create contract tests for every public Execution plane interface.
Create integration tests with every supported adjacent layer and execution tier.
Create compatibility tests across supported CPU architectures, runtimes, hypervisors, providers, and protocol versions relevant to Execution plane.
Fuzz parsers, schemas, protocol handlers, WIT/RPC boundaries, or untrusted inputs handled by Execution plane.
Create concurrency and race-condition tests for shared/distributed Execution plane state.
Create security tests derived directly from the Execution plane threat model.
Create benchmark, soak, burst, and fleet-scale tests appropriate to Execution plane.
Create disaster, partition, reconnect, and degraded-control-plane tests.
Require machine-readable acceptance evidence before certifying a Execution plane release for production.
Define production SLOs, error budgets, and support commitments for Execution plane.
Define canary, staged rollout, rollback, and emergency-disable procedures for Execution plane.
Maintain a supported-version compatibility matrix for Execution plane and adjacent dependencies.
Define patching, vulnerability response, and end-of-life SLAs for Execution plane.
Provide backup, restore, migration, or reconstruction procedures for Execution plane state where applicable.
Create day-0 bootstrap, day-1 deployment, and day-2 operation runbooks.
Define incident severity, paging, escalation, containment, and recovery procedures.
Perform recurring access, policy, dependency, configuration, and architecture reviews.
Track exceptions, waivers, technical debt, and deprecated behaviors with owners and expiry dates.
Require a formal production exit gate confirming architecture, requirements, interfaces, implementation, security, resilience, performance, observability, testing, rollback, and ownership readiness.
